description: Rules for an AI coding agent to filter out generic AI-generated UI designs, text, and code.

latest_release.name: v3.2.29: Muse Code becomes the ninth plugin door
latest_release.body:
**Muse Code becomes the ninth plugin door, and it needed no new manifest.** Set one experimental flag, add the repository as a marketplace, and Muse imports all six skills from a manifest it already understands.

## It needed no new manifest

Muse Code looks for an Agent Plugins root `plugin.json` first, then `.muse-plugin/`, then `.claude-plugin/`. The repository root carries only a name, so Muse selects `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, the same file Claude Code reads.

No `.muse-plugin` folder was added. A second manifest would be a version to bump every release and a claim that something is wired up when it is not.

The plugin system sits behind an opt-in flag, so the install sets it first:

```bash
export MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS=1
muse plugins marketplace add anti-slop miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop
muse plugins install antislop@anti-slop
```

On Windows, set `$env:MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS = "1"` in PowerShell instead. Muse ships a native Windows installer, so the flag is not a macOS and Linux detail.

Skills load with the plugin. The contrast MCP server is a runtime capability, so it needs `muse plugins approve antislop`, and any package change resets that approval.

## A separator that mattered

Muse rejected the six skills' `allowed-tools` frontmatter, which used spaces, and it rejected the whole plugin with it: a marketplace snapshot reported `plugins=0 skipped=1`, so the door offered nothing at all. The field is now comma-separated in all six skills and in the generator that produces the core.

The Agent Skills specification shows the space-separated form, and Claude Code accepts either. Muse accepts commas only. No single form satisfies every parser, so the comma form was chosen: Muse keeps the plugin, Claude Code reads the tools correctly, and a parser that follows the specification literally grants no pre-approval, which changes nothing except permission prompts.

## The installer covers it too

Muse Code reads `.agents/skills` at both scopes, plus `.claude/skills` and `.codex/skills` in a project, with the shared folder outranking the other two. The installer already writes that shared folder, so Muse joins without a new path. The installer now covers fourteen agents over nine folders.

The duplicate-read warning knows about Muse too, so picking it beside Claude Code or Codex names the second copy before a skill silently loses to one of them.

Project skills are gated by a trust decision. The first `muse` run asks whether to trust the workspace and remembers the answer; until then the skills stay dark and `muse skills list` reports `project-skills-untrusted`. A global install and the plugin door are not gated.

## What is verified, and what is not

Verified on Muse Code 1.4.15 in WSL. The shorthand source resolves to GitHub, the GitHub marketplace now offers 3.2.29, the install imports all six skills with activation on, `muse plugins approve` enables the contrast server, and an MCP `check_contrast` call returned a real ratio. Duplicate skill ids were used to confirm the folder order: `.agents/skills` wins, then `.codex/skills`, then `.claude/skills`.

The installer smoke test pins the Muse target paths, its global target, and the duplicate read.

Two things are not verified: a full Muse session with a signed-in account, since this machine has no Meta account, and a session on Windows. Both need an account and a live session, so they stay unclaimed rather than assumed.

## Updating

```bash
muse plugins marketplace update anti-slop
muse plugins update antislop
muse plugins approve antislop
```

A changed package resets the approval, so the last line is needed again after every update. Removing the plugin is `muse plugins remove antislop`, and removing the marketplace as well is `muse plugins marketplace remove anti-slop`.

The installer route is unchanged:

```bash
npx antislop-ai --update
```

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/antislop-ai?style=flat-square&color=cb3837&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/antislop-ai) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-20.12%2B-339933?style=flat-square&logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white)](cli/package.json) [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop?style=flat-square)](https://skills.sh/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-f4c430?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/VWKggJfHFR) # Anti Slop: Rules for AI Coding Agents ### A rulebook that stops an AI coding agent shipping generic UI, text, and AI-shaped code. **A filter, not a style guide.** No prescribed colors, fonts, or layouts, and direction stays yours. **[Website](https://antislop.ai.id) · [Guide](GUIDE.md) · [Install](https://antislop.ai.id/install)** [Before and after](#before-and-after) · [Install](#install) · [What it does](#what-it-does) · [Skills](#skills) · [FAQ](#faq) npx antislop-ai
--- ## Before and after Each pair below is one brief, run twice, so the difference is visible side by side. ### UI With /antislop-ui. antislop alone is not the after. It removes the slop and stops there; direction comes from `DESIGN.md`. For UI work you intend to ship, that file is mandatory: without it the result is labelled a draft without direction. The pair below is the result. | **Before: without antislop** | **After: antislop + `DESIGN.md`** | |:--|:--| | | | | This is what most AI output looks like: slop everywhere once you take a closer look. | Much better. antislop kills the slop, and `DESIGN.md` gives it a real visual direction. | The two partial states are worth seeing, because each one shows why the other half matters: | **Partial: antislop alone** | **Partial: `DESIGN.md` alone** | |:--|:--| | | | | The slop is gone, but so is the direction. That is why antislop needs a `DESIGN.md`. | The direction is there, but honestly it is still far from good: the slop still shows. | ### Copywriting With /antislop-copywriting. One prompt, run twice. ### Accessibility With /antislop-human. One sign-in form, run twice. ### Mobile layout With /antislop-layoutmobile. One dashboard on a phone, run twice. ### Code With /antislop-code. One file, run twice. Every image here opens full size if you click it. ## Install antislop ships as standard agent skills: one folder per skill, holding a `SKILL.md`. Installation differs per agent, so pick the section for the one you use. Each route is walked through from zero, with update and removal, in [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md#install-update-and-remove). ### The installer (recommended) One command, then answer the prompts. It asks which skills you want, where to install them (this project or everywhere), and which agents you use, then copies the folders and writes the pointer that reloads antislop every session. ```bash npx antislop-ai ``` ### The skills directory antislop is listed on [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop), the open directory for agent skills. This copies the same folders as the installer and nothing else, so antislop reloads by description alone. ```bash npx skills add miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop ``` ### Claude Code - Plugin ```text /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop /plugin install antislop@anti-slop ``` ### Antigravity - Plugin ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop ``` ### Codex - Plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop codex plugin add antislop@anti-slop ``` ### Cursor - Plugin ```bash agent plugin marketplace add https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop ``` Then open **Customize**, find **antislop**, and select **Install**. ### Kimi Code - Plugin ```text /plugins install https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop ``` ### DeepSeek Harness - Plugin Open **Plugins**, choose **Add plugin**, paste this package name, and select **Install**: ```text antislop-ai ``` That is the desktop route. From a terminal instead, name the profile you use: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add antislop-ai ``` ### Cline - Plugin ```bash cline plugin install https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop.git ``` This door covers the Cline CLI. For the VS Code or JetBrains extension, use the installer. ### Muse Code - Plugin Muse Code keeps its plugin system behind an opt-in flag, so set it first. On macOS and Linux: ```bash export MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS=1 muse plugins marketplace add anti-slop miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop muse plugins install antislop@anti-slop ``` On Windows, set `$env:MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS = "1"` in PowerShell first, then run the two `muse` lines unchanged. Skills load without another step. Run `muse plugins approve antislop` to enable the contrast MCP server. ### Oh My Pi - Plugin ```bash omp plugin marketplace add miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop omp plugin install antislop@anti-slop ``` ### Pi - Package ```bash pi install git:github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop ``` ### The single file `antislop.md` on its own is a complete filter you can paste into any chat window, with no packaging and no folders. ```bash curl -o antislop.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop/main/antislop.md ``` ## What it does - **40 mandatory rules** (R-01 to R-40) in three tiers: Hard Gate, Purpose-Gate, and Quality Locks. - **A Liveliness Toolkit**: three dials (ENERGY / RHYTHM / MOTION) and a Design Read, so the result comes out alive rather than merely clean. - **A Delivery Gate**: a mandatory PASS/FAIL report in four blocks, run before anything ships. - **Six skills**, one per concern, so an agent loads only what a task needs. The core prevents slop but cannot invent direction. `DESIGN.md` (yours) supplies it, and a sterile result means the direction was missing, not that the filter failed (R-37). antislop never beautifies on its own. ## Skills | Skill | Covers | Pick it for | |-------|--------|-------------| | antislop | The core filter: rules, tiers, the Delivery Gate, liveliness | Everything. Always loaded | | antislop-ui | Layout, color, components, decoration, motion, structure, performance | UI and visual work | | antislop-copywriting | Headlines, CTAs, tone, fake stats, anti-AI writing, markdown hygiene | Copy and text | | antislop-human | Contrast, keyboard, focus, states, interaction affordances | Accessibility | | antislop-layoutmobile | Reflow across screen widths, breakpoints, grids, overflow, tap targets | Responsive work | | antislop-code | AI-slop comments: which to remove, which to keep | Comment cleanup | Install one, several, or the core alone. ## Usage modes antislop runs one of two ways, and by default the agent asks which at the start of every session. Both end with a report you can check; they differ in when the rules apply. - **During** guides the work while it is built, and the session closes with the Delivery Gate report. Use it when you are building something new. - **After** audits work that already exists: a numbered findings list, you approve which to fix, then a follow-up report. Use it to clean up output you already have. Saving a preference is opt-in. With no settings file, antislop keeps asking in every new session exactly as it does today. Save your preferred mode once to skip that question: ```bash npx antislop-ai --mode during ``` Use `after` instead for audits, `ask` to restore the question in every session, or `--mode` alone to view the setting. The file is shared, so one command covers every agent and every project: `~/.config/antislop/settings.json` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%\antislop\settings.json` on Windows. A mode you ask for in the current chat always wins for that session and never changes what is saved. When a saved preference applies, the skill says so once: **"antislop active: during (global preference)."** Older installs still carry the unconditional question, so run the update below to pick this up. ## Update antislop does not update itself. If you installed through the installer, one command replaces what is already there, in this project and under your home directory, and prints the release it replaced: ```bash npx antislop-ai --update ``` A plugin keeps its own copy under the agent that installed it, so it updates through its own command, and the Pi package updates through Pi. Every route is listed in [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md#install-update-and-remove). Skills load when a session starts, so start a new one afterwards. ## FAQ **Is antislop a style guide?** No, a filter. It rejects technique without purpose and requires liveliness. Direction is yours. **Which agents does it work with?** Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cursor, Cline, Amp, Gemini CLI, Hermes, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code, DeepSeek Harness, Muse Code, Pi, and Oh My Pi. The installer covers fourteen of them and detects which ones you have, and the plugin doors install from this same repository. [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md) lists the folder each agent reads. **What is a skill?** A folder that goes deeper into one concern, holding a `SKILL.md` with its rules. Skills reference the core rules by number and never duplicate them, so adding one does not change the core. ## Roadmap **v3.2.29** adds Muse Code as the ninth plugin door: - **Shared folder.** Muse Code reads `.agents/skills` at both scopes, the folder Antigravity, Copilot, Kimi Code, Amp, and DeepSeek Harness already share. - **One more step.** Muse Code keeps its plugin system behind `MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS=1`, and the install section names that first. Every earlier release, and what comes next, is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop&type=Date)](https://star-history.com/#miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop&Date) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps make antislop better.

Found a new slop pattern, a rule that missed something, or a bug in the installer? Open an [issue](https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop/issues). What a pull request has to carry is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and behavior in issues and pull requests is covered by [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

“antislop is a filter, not magic.
It clears the slop from your UI, text, and code.
A beautiful UI is DESIGN.md's job, and yours.”

## Disclaimer Get antislop from [miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop](https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop), [antislop.ai.id](https://antislop.ai.id), or the [antislop-ai npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/antislop-ai). The npm name `antislop` belongs to a different package, so `npx antislop` does not install this project. There is no antislop coin, token, or fundraising.
